Steeped in history, the town is mentioned in the Domesday Book and is home to one of the oldest markets in Derbyshire, the Charter Market, which was established by Henry III. Today, Ripley is a bustling town with a mix of high street and independent shops alongside parks and green spaces. With a variety of local events throughout the year, the town has a strong sense of community that is reflected in our development. Ripley is just nine miles from Derby city centre via the A38 and around twelve miles from Nottingham. It also offers easy access to junction 28 of the M1. There are regular bus services to Derby and Nottingham, and a train station in the nearby town of Alfreton with a direct train to Manchester Piccadilly station. East Midlands Airport is also within easy reach. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the stunning landscapes of the Peak District National Park and the Cromford World Heritage Site are only around 30 minutes away.
